title: 'Paranormal Activity - A New Story Live is an edge-of-your-seat thrill-ride'
excerpt: Paranormal Activity: A New Story Live on Broadway is undoubtedly one of the best shows I have ever seen on the stage. It perfectly pairs horror and humor and I think it has the power to inspire a whole new generation of theater-goers
content:
Paranormal Activity: A New Story Live on Broadway is undoubtedly one of the best shows I have ever seen on the stage. It perfectly pairs horror and humor and I think it has the power to inspire a whole new generation of theater-goers

17:49 ET, 12 Sep 2026Updated 18:44 ET, 12 Sep 2026

When I first heard that Paranormal Activity had hit Broadway, I couldn't quite imagine how they'd bring such an iconic horror franchise to the stage.

‌

Would it be just a reimagining of Katie and Micah's story from the first movie in the series that is nearly 20 years old?

For those who have been living under a metaphorical horror rock for the last two decades, the 2007 blockbuster hit, which had a meagre budget of just $15,000, made over $193.4million at the global box office, and brought a fresh and terrifying perspective to the horror movie industry.

Article continues below

The bone-chilling blockbuster sees young couple Katie (Katie Featherston) and Micah (Micah Sloat) move into a home in suburban San Diego, California, hoping to start building a life together. But things take a terrifying turn as the pair become increasingly troubled by a haunting nightly presence, which they believe to be evil.

‌

Cut to Paranormal Activity: A New Story Live on Broadway, and we're introduced to another young couple: James (Travis A. Knight) and Lou (Cher Álvarez), who have moved to London, England, from Chicago, U.S., in search of a fresh start after Lou begins experiencing a series of blackouts and unexplained occurrences.

The millennial couple seem determined to make a go of it in their cozy two-story home, complete with an Amazon Alexa, which Lou eagerly uses to listen to the chilling podcast of paranormal scientist Etheline Cotgrave (Eva Kaminsky).

‌

But things soon start to go awry, as more unexplained occurrences begin to unfold, leaving Lou convinced that she's being haunted. Almost as terrifying, however, is James's overbearing mother Carolanne (Shannon Cochran), who regularly contacts them via video calls but hilariously hasn't quite figured out how to hold up her cellphone without covering the camera with her thumb.

It's one of the many things I think the production gets exactly right: a quick-witted, relatable sense of humor that provides a welcome shift in tone amid the horror. The comedy never undermines the scares; instead, it makes the darker moments feel even more effective. At several points, I found myself watching the show through my hands (a tell-tale sign of an excellent horror!).

Unexplained occurrences, from power outages to ominous bangings on their quintessentially British stained-glass-panelled front door, soon begin to plague the couple. James initially shrugs off Lou's concerns, convinced that London's National Grid simply can't get its s--t together. But before long, even he becomes disturbed.

‌

What follows is a symphony of all things scary, as Lou begins to act increasingly strangely and the unexplained happenings become ever more frequent. And speaking of symphonies, full credit must go to sound designer Gareth Fry, who has created an incredible soundscape that, unlike a traditional score, feels almost like an additional actor in this four-person show. It perfectly heightens the tension and contributes to the ever-increasing sense of dread.

But undoubtedly, the most mind-blowing element of the show has to be its effects. The visual effects artists previously worked on Harry Potter and the Cursed Child — and it shows (for those who know, know). Their work here is nothing short of brilliant.

‌

One of the production's most incredible moments comes when James is speaking to Lou in the kitchen about his day, while she stands with her back to him. After some time, however, Lou walks down the stairs and asks James, "Who were you talking to?" It's then that the robed figure in the kitchen suddenly disappears, and James is left with the terrifying realization that he wasn't speaking to his wife at all.

Even now, I can't comprehend how they were able to pull that off — and quite honestly, I don't want to. It was one of the most jaw-dropping things I've ever seen on stage.

More chilling visual effects and shocking frights follow, including James's mother transforming from Southern Belle to Southern Hell, with Cochran delivering a devastatingly disturbing performance.

The terror and fear continue to build as James and Lou, once a seemingly unshakeable power couple, watch their marriage become increasingly strained as they struggle to cope with what is happening within their four walls. Flashing lights and booming music erupt into a final, thunderous crescendo, leaving the audience audibly gasping as James and Lou finally uncover why they have been haunted by this terrifying presence.

I can wholeheartedly say that Paranormal Activity: A New Story Live is the most unique play I have ever seen. At a time when reports suggest many Broadway shows are struggling to fill their seats night after night, I genuinely believe this production has the power to revolutionize Broadway and inspire a new generation to take an interest in theater.

One minor criticism I've seen online concerns the seating. I was seated near the front, which undoubtedly added to the terror, as I could see James and Lou's petrified expressions up close. However, it also meant I couldn't see some of the terrifying events unfolding on the second story of the house quite as clearly. That didn't impact my experience at all, though. In fact, I think it's rather ingenious that audiences seated in different parts of the auditorium can leave the theater completely terrified by entirely different moments, depending on their perspective.

I would wholeheartedly recommend that everyone go and see this spectacular show at least once — although, honestly, I could watch it multiple times over. Paranormal Activity: A New Story Live is a spine-chilling, edge-of-your-seat thrill ride that completely flips the traditional theater experience on its head. If this is the future of Broadway, I can't wait to see what's next.
